text: (including vinorelbine, gemcitabine, taxanes, and irinotecan), platinum-based regimens still have a high- er response, but they cause more toxicity and 1-year sur- vival is not significantly different.35 In general, cisplatin- based chemotherapy has become the standard of care for advanced disease,2,12-15,30 although no particular regimen has been identified as superior.36,37 Regimens include cis- platin or carboplatin combined with either gemcitabine, ir- inotecan, etoposide, vinblastine, vinorelbine, docetaxel, or paclitaxel.14,15 Older triple regimens such as mitomycin, vinblastine, and cisplatin (MVP) or mitomycin, ifosfa- mide, and cisplatin (MIC) are no better and are no longer advocated.12,37 A combination of carboplatin and paclitax- el with the monoclonal antibody bevacizumab may be an option for patients with non-squamous cell histology and good performance status.14 For patients who fail initial therapy for advanced disease, docetaxel13,14,30 as a single agent is generally recommended for second-line treat- ment. Alternative drugs that may be considered include er- lotinib, gemcitabine, or pemetrexed.12-15,38,39 Topotecan is also under investigation.40 Despite initial promise, disap- pointing results using gefitinib either alone15,41 or with platinum-based chemotherapy42,43 have been reported. The success of gefitinib may depend on identifying pa- tients with specific mutations of the epidermal growth fac- tor receptor (EGFR) gene.44 Bronchoscopic photodynamic therapy, with porfimer so- dium, may be considered for the palliative treatment of bronchial obstruction.14,45 Photodynamic therapy may also be used as an alternative to surgery in patients with very early-stage (in situ) endobronchial NSCLC.45 Other palliative options for obstructed airways include endo- bronchial brachytherapy or stent placement, or laser treat- ment. External beam radiotherapy may be useful for symptom control and surgery may be suitable in some cas- es of resectable local recurrence.14 Despite the recent advances in chemotherapy for NSCLC, the median survival for this disease remains poor, and there is a need to identify alternative approaches to treat- ment. Those in preclinical development include gene therapy46 with the tumour suppressor gene p53, and cancer vaccine immunotherapy.47 Given the poor prognosis of lung cancers, and the high in- cidence of second primaries in patients curatively treated for early-stage disease, there has been great interest in prophylaxis.
